points.title: What a data dictionary is
points.must: A document or table that describes the structure of a database — data about the data (metadata); for every table it lists every field.

points.title: When it is written
points.must: During the design stage, before the database is built, and kept up to date while the system is used.

points.title: What it records for each field
points.must: At least five of: field name, data type, field size, format, key (PK/FK), validation rule, required / null, description, example.

points.title: An example entry
points.must: A field described in full, e.g. DateOfBirth — Date — 10 — DD/MM/YYYY — validation range — example 14/03/2009.

points.title: Purpose: one agreed definition
points.must: Everyone uses the same field names, types and sizes, so the data is consistent and keys match between tables.

points.title: Purpose: building and testing
points.must: Helps programmers create the tables and write SQL / forms correctly; records the validation rules; testers choose test data from them.

points.title: Who uses it
points.must: Designers / analysts, programmers, testers and database administrators.

points.title: System catalogue
points.must: A DBMS keeps its own internal data dictionary, updated automatically: tables, fields, keys, indexes and user permissions.
